# UpstreamSync

> Julia tooling that keeps the JuliaGiac forks (main = pristine upstream tree tagged upstream/X.Y.Z, dev = our fork) in sync with Bernard Parisse's Giac release tarballs: check for releases, import a tarball as a tagged commit, plan the merge into dev, export our fixes as GitHub commit links.


# UpstreamSync

Julia tooling that keeps the JuliaGiac forks in sync with Bernard Parisse's
upstream releases of [Giac](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~parisse/giac.html).

Upstream does not use a public version control system: releases are
published as tarballs (`giac-X.Y.Z.tar.gz`) with an `md5sum.txt` in
<https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~parisse/giac/>. This project
turns each tarball into a tagged commit of the fork, prepares the merge of
that release into our fork, and lists our fixes so that they can be sent
back upstream.

Nothing here ever pushes, opens pull requests or posts anything: every
command works on a local clone and prints the next steps.

## The main/dev convention

Each fork (configured in [`upstreams.toml`](https://github.com/JuliaGiac/upstream-sync/blob/main/upstreams.toml)) has two
long-lived branches:

| Branch | Content |
|---|---|
| `main` | the **pristine upstream tree**, one commit per imported release, imported from the release tarball through a pull request and tagged `upstream/X.Y.Z` once merged. The only non-upstream files are the *kept paths* (for giac: `.github/`, the Dependabot configuration). |
| `dev` | **our fork**: Meson build, fixes, tests, site, CI. Upstream releases reach `dev` by merging `main` (or the import branch). |

So `git diff upstream/X.Y.Z dev` is exactly "what we changed", and
`git diff upstream/A upstream/B` is exactly "what upstream changed".

Only `giac` ([JuliaGiac/giac](https://github.com/JuliaGiac/giac)) is
configured. On its `dev` branch, MicroPython (`micropython/`, replacing
upstream's vendored `micropython-1.12/`) and the Xcas FLTK GUI
([s-celles/xcas](https://github.com/s-celles/xcas), extracted from the giac
tarball) are git submodules and are **deliberately not synced** with
upstream: Giac.jl only needs libgiac. Their upstream paths, like the
autotools files replaced by Meson, are listed in `fork_excluded_paths` so
that `merge-plan` treats upstream changes to them as expected.

## Installation

Requirements: Julia ≥ 1.10, `git` ≥ 2.28 and `tar` (with `gzip`/`bzip2`/`xz`)
on the `PATH`.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/JuliaGiac/upstream-sync.git
cd upstream-sync
julia --project=. -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.instantiate()'    # or: just instantiate
```

## Contents

- [Commands](commands.md) and [exit status](commands.md#Exit-status)
- [Release procedure](release.md)
- [Configuration](configuration.md)
- [API](api.md)


# Commands

```text
julia --project=. bin/upstream-sync.jl [--config FILE] [--cache DIR] <command> ...
```

With [just](https://github.com/casey/just): `just check`, `just import giac
2.1.0 ../giac`, `just tag giac 2.1.0 ../giac`, `just merge-plan giac 2.1.0
../giac`, `just export giac ../giac`.

## `check [NAME] [--repo PATH|URL] [--github-output]`

Lists the release versions found in the upstream index, the latest one and
the latest imported one (the highest `upstream/X.Y.Z` tag, read with
`git ls-remote --tags` from the GitHub repository, or from `--repo`), and
reports whether a newer release exists. Without `NAME`, every configured
upstream is checked. `--github-output` appends
`new_releases=<name> <X.Y.Z>,...` and `status=...` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`.

## `import NAME X.Y.Z --repo PATH [--force] [--offline] [--allow-stale]`

In a local clone of the fork:

1. downloads `giac-X.Y.Z.tar.gz` and `md5sum.txt` (the tarball is cached in
   `cache/`, or `$UPSTREAM_SYNC_CACHE`, and reused; the checksum file is
   always refreshed unless `--offline`) and verifies the checksum;
2. extracts the tarball and strips its top directory;
3. creates the branch `upstream-import/X.Y.Z` from `main` with one commit
   whose tree is **exactly** the tarball (bytes as published: no
   `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes` or end-of-line filtering; file modes from
   the tar headers) plus the kept paths of `main`. The commit is
   "import upstream giac X.Y.Z", with the source URL, the checksum and the
   tree hash (`Tree: <hash>`) in its body; author and committer are your
   local git identity.

It does **not** tag: the pull request may be merged with a method that
rewrites the commit (squash, rebase), so the tag is created afterwards by
`tag`.

The working tree and index of the clone are not touched (the commit is
built with a temporary index). Nothing is pushed; the next steps are
printed. `--force` replaces an existing branch and tag.

The import refuses to start when the local `main` differs from `main` on
`origin` (read with `git ls-remote origin`): an import based on a stale
`main` would, for instance, drop the kept `.github/` files committed since.
Update it first (`git fetch origin main:main`) or pass `--allow-stale`.

## `tag NAME X.Y.Z --repo PATH [--force] [--offline]`

Run once the import pull request is merged, **with any merge method**:

1. fetches `main` from `origin` (unless `--offline`);
2. finds the commit of `origin/main` with the tree of the import: the
   import commit itself if it is on `main` (merge commit, fast-forward),
   otherwise the oldest commit with the same tree (squash, rebase). The
   import tree is read from the `upstream-import/X.Y.Z` branch (local or
   `origin/`), or, if that branch was deleted, from the "import upstream
   giac X.Y.Z" commit on `main` (its `Tree:` line, or its own tree);
3. creates the annotated tag `upstream/X.Y.Z` there, with the source URL
   and checksum of the import.

It refuses when no commit of `main` has that tree (pull request not merged
yet) or when `upstream/X.Y.Z` already exists on another commit (`--force`
moves it); it is a no-op when the tag is already right. It prints the
`git push origin upstream/X.Y.Z` command and never pushes.

## `merge-plan NAME X.Y.Z --repo PATH [--output FILE] [--force] [--allow-stale] [--resolve-expected [--worktree DIR]]`

Creates the branch `sync/X.Y.Z` from `dev`, tries
`git merge --no-commit upstream-import/X.Y.Z` on it (in a temporary
worktree), aborts the merge, and writes a Markdown report
(`merge-plan-<name>-X.Y.Z.md` by default) with:

- the files changed upstream (added/modified/deleted, lines, per area);
- the upstream changes touching files we modified on `dev`;
- the **expected conflicts**: "deleted by us" conflicts on
  `fork_excluded_paths` (files `dev` intentionally does not carry, such as
  `micropython-1.12/`, the Xcas GUI sources and the autotools build), to be
  resolved by keeping the deletion;
- the **excluded additions**: files upstream added under
  `fork_excluded_paths`. `git merge` adds them to `dev` without a conflict
  (2.1.0 brought back ten `micropython-1.12/` files this way), so they are
  listed apart, to be removed;
- the **new upstream files** outside `fork_excluded_paths`: they merge
  cleanly, but the Meson build may need to list them (2.1.0 added
  `src/proba.cc` and its test);
- the **real conflicts** grouped by area: Meson/build, src fixes, docs,
  other (areas are configured in `upstreams.toml`), with their kind
  ("both modified", "deleted by us", ...).

Like `import`, it refuses a local `dev` that differs from `origin`'s unless
`--allow-stale`.

With `--resolve-expected`, the merge is not aborted: it is left in progress
in a worktree of `sync/X.Y.Z` (default: `<repo>-sync-X.Y.Z` next to the
clone, or `--worktree DIR`), with the expected conflicts and the excluded
additions removed by `git rm` and the real conflicts still marked. Nothing is committed: finish the
merge there, then `git worktree remove` it.

## `export NAME --repo PATH [--output FILE]`

Lists our changes to the upstream sources, as Markdown: the commits of
`dev` that are not on `main` and modify the configured source paths (for
giac `src/` and `check/`, without `meson.build` files), oldest first, each
with date, hash, subject and GitHub URL
(`https://github.com/JuliaGiac/giac/commit/<hash>`), and the diffstat of
`main...dev` on those paths. This is what the maintainer sends upstream as
links.

## Exit status

| Status | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| 0 | success; for `check`: every upstream is up to date |
| 1 | error (message on stderr) |
| 10 | `check` only: a release newer than the latest `upstream/X.Y.Z` tag exists |


# Release procedure

The weekly workflow [`check-upstream.yml`](https://github.com/JuliaGiac/upstream-sync/blob/main/.github/workflows/check-upstream.yml)
runs `check` and opens (or updates) an issue "New upstream release: giac
X.Y.Z" in this repository. Then, for giac X.Y.Z:

1. **Check** (optional, the issue already did it):
   `julia --project=. bin/upstream-sync.jl check giac`
2. **Import** into an up-to-date clone of the fork:
   ```sh
   git -C ../giac fetch origin && git -C ../giac branch -f main origin/main
   julia --project=. bin/upstream-sync.jl import giac X.Y.Z --repo ../giac
   ```
   Review it: `git -C ../giac show --stat upstream-import/X.Y.Z`.
3. **Publish the import** (this tool never pushes):
   ```sh
   git -C ../giac push origin upstream-import/X.Y.Z
   gh pr create --repo JuliaGiac/giac --base main --head upstream-import/X.Y.Z \
     --title "import upstream giac X.Y.Z"
   ```
   Merge that pull request with **any** method (merge commit, squash or
   rebase).
4. **Tag the merged commit**, then push the tag:
   ```sh
   julia --project=. bin/upstream-sync.jl tag giac X.Y.Z --repo ../giac
   git -C ../giac push origin upstream/X.Y.Z
   ```
   `check` reads these `upstream/X.Y.Z` tags as the imported versions.
5. **Plan the fork update** (with `dev` up to date: `git -C ../giac pull --ff-only`):
   ```sh
   julia --project=. bin/upstream-sync.jl merge-plan giac X.Y.Z --repo ../giac \
     --resolve-expected
   ```
   Read `merge-plan-giac-X.Y.Z.md`: expected and real conflicts, excluded
   additions, upstream changes on files we patched, and the new upstream
   files (add new sources and tests to the Meson build). A "deleted by us" real conflict is a file
   `dev` removed outside `fork_excluded_paths`: keep the deletion or restore
   the file, and update `fork_excluded_paths` if the removal is intended.
6. **Merge into dev**: in the worktree `../giac-sync-X.Y.Z` (branch
   `sync/X.Y.Z`, merge in progress, expected conflicts and excluded
   additions already removed),
   resolve the real conflicts, bump the version in `meson.build`, run the
   tests, `git commit`, push `sync/X.Y.Z` and open a pull request to `dev`.
   Then `git -C ../giac worktree remove ../giac-sync-X.Y.Z`.
7. **Send our fixes upstream**:
   `julia --project=. bin/upstream-sync.jl export giac --repo ../giac --output fixes.md`
   and send the links of the relevant commits to Bernard Parisse.
8. Close the issue.


# Configuration

Upstreams are configured in `upstreams.toml` at the root of the project
(another file can be given with `--config FILE`). Each table describes one
fork:

```toml
[giac]
repo = "JuliaGiac/giac"
upstream_branch = "main"
fork_branch = "dev"
index_url = "https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~parisse/giac/"
release_regex = '^giac-(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)\.tar\.gz$'
release_file = "giac-{version}.tar.gz"
checksum_file = "md5sum.txt"
checksum_algorithm = "md5"
keep_paths = [".github/"]
export_paths = ["src/", "check/"]
export_exclude = ["**/meson.build"]
export_modified_only = true
fork_excluded_paths = ["micropython-1.12/", "src/hist.*", "/configure", "..."]

[giac.areas]
build = ["meson.build", "configure.ac", "m4/", "..."]
src = ["src/"]
docs = ["doc/", "*.md", "..."]
```

| Key | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | yes | | GitHub repository of the fork (`owner/name`), used for `git ls-remote` and commit URLs |
| `index_url` | yes | | HTML directory listing where releases appear |
| `release_regex` | yes | | file names that are releases; capture group 1 is the `X.Y.Z` version |
| `release_file` | yes | | tarball name of a version, `{version}` is replaced by `X.Y.Z` |
| `checksum_file` | yes | | checksum list (`<hex>  <file>` lines) next to the tarballs |
| `checksum_algorithm` | | `md5` | `md5`, `sha1`, `sha256` or `sha512` |
| `download_url` | | `index_url` | base URL of the tarballs and checksum file (`file://` works) |
| `upstream_branch` | | `main` | branch with the pristine upstream tree |
| `fork_branch` | | `dev` | branch with the fork |
| `tag_prefix` | | `upstream/` | prefix of the release tags |
| `import_branch_prefix` | | `upstream-import/` | prefix of the import branches |
| `sync_branch_prefix` | | `sync/` | prefix of the merge-plan branches |
| `keep_paths` | | `[]` | paths of the upstream branch carried over by every import (`dir/` = folder); a tarball file inside them is dropped and listed in the commit message |
| `export_paths` | | `[]` | git pathspecs of the upstream sources whose changes are "our fixes" |
| `export_exclude` | | `[]` | git glob pathspecs removed from `export_paths` |
| `export_modified_only` | | `true` | only count modifications of files that exist upstream, not files we added or deleted |
| `fork_excluded_paths` | | `[]` | upstream files the fork branch intentionally does not carry; `merge-plan` reports a "deleted by us" conflict on them as expected (keep the deletion) rather than as a real conflict, and lists the files upstream adds under them (merged without a conflict) to be removed |
| `areas.build`, `areas.src`, `areas.docs` | | `[]` | patterns grouping merge-plan files; first match wins in the order build, src, docs; anything else is "other" |

Patterns (`areas`, `fork_excluded_paths`): `dir/` matches everything below
`dir/`; a pattern containing `/` is a glob on the whole path; a pattern
without `/` (`meson.build`, `*.md`) matches the file name at any depth; a
leading `/` anchors the pattern at the root (`/configure` is only the
top-level `configure`, `/mk*` matches `mkosx` but not `src/mkfoo`); `*`, `?`
and `**` are globs.

For giac, `fork_excluded_paths` lists what `dev` removed from the upstream
tree on purpose: `micropython-1.12/` (a submodule `micropython/` on `dev`),
the Xcas FLTK GUI sources (moved to s-celles/xcas, a submodule), the
autotools build replaced by Meson, legacy platform scripts and packaging,
and the plain-text docs converted to Markdown. MicroPython and Xcas are not
synced with upstream: Giac.jl only needs libgiac.

Branches are looked up as local branches first, then as `origin/<branch>`.
`import` (upstream branch) and `merge-plan` (fork branch) compare that ref
with the branch on `origin` (`git ls-remote origin`) and refuse a stale one
unless `--allow-stale`; without an `origin` remote only a note is printed.

## Environment

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `UPSTREAM_SYNC_CACHE` | download cache (default: `cache/` in the project, ignored by git); `--cache DIR` overrides it. Tarballs are stored as `<cache>/<name>/<file>`; extraction and merge worktrees are created in `<cache>/work/` and removed afterwards. |
| `GITHUB_OUTPUT` | file to which `check --github-output` appends its results |


# API

The command line tool is a thin wrapper around these functions; they can
also be used from Julia (`using UpstreamSync`).

## Entry points

### `UpstreamSync`

nothing

### `UpstreamSync.main`

main(args; io=stdout) -> Int

Command line entry point (see `bin/upstream-sync.jl` and
[`ExitCode`](@ref)). Returns the exit status instead of exiting.

### `UpstreamSync.ExitCode`

Exit status of the `upstream-sync` command line tool.

- `ExitCode.OK` (0): success; for `check`, every upstream is up to date.
- `ExitCode.ERROR` (1): an error occurred.
- `ExitCode.NEW_RELEASE` (10): `check` found an upstream release newer than
  the latest `upstream/X.Y.Z` tag.

### `check`

check(u; repo=nothing, io=stdout, index_html=nothing) -> CheckResult

List the upstream releases (from `u.index_url`, or the given `index_html`),
the latest one and the latest imported one; report whether a newer release
exists.

### `import_release`

import_release(u, version; repo, cache=cache_dir(), io=stdout,
                   force=false, offline=false, allow_stale=false) -> ImportResult

Import an upstream release tarball into the local clone `repo`:
download (cached) and verify it, then create the commit
"import upstream <name> X.Y.Z" whose tree is the tarball's content (top
directory stripped) plus the kept paths of the upstream branch, on the new
branch `upstream-import/X.Y.Z` (parent: the upstream branch). The body
records the source URL, the checksum and the tree hash (`Tree: <hash>`).
Author and committer are the local git identity. No tag is created: once
the pull request is merged (with any method), [`tag_release`](@ref) tags
the commit of the upstream branch that has this tree. The working tree is not touched and nothing is pushed.
With `force`, an existing branch and tag are replaced. The import refuses
to start when the local upstream branch differs from `origin`'s, unless
`allow_stale` (see [`check_not_stale`](@ref)).

### `tag_release`

tag_release(u, version; repo, io=stdout, force=false, offline=false)
        -> TagResult

Run after the import pull request is merged, with any merge method. Fetch
the upstream branch from `origin` (unless `offline`; without an `origin`
remote the local branch is used), then find on it the commit with the tree
of the import:

- the import commit itself if it is on the branch (merge commit or
  fast-forward);
- otherwise the oldest commit with the same tree (squash or rebase merge).

The import tree is read from the import branch (`upstream-import/X.Y.Z`,
local or `origin/`), or, once that branch is deleted, from the
"import upstream <name> X.Y.Z" commit on the upstream branch: the `Tree:`
line of its message, or else (imports made before that line existed) its
own tree. Create the annotated tag `upstream/X.Y.Z` there, with the source URL
and checksum of the import. Refuse when no commit matches, or when the tag
already exists on another commit (unless `force`). Never pushes.

### `merge_plan`

merge_plan(u, version; repo, cache=cache_dir(), output=nothing,
               io=stdout, force=false, allow_stale=false,
               resolve_expected=false, worktree=nothing) -> MergePlan

Create the branch `sync/X.Y.Z` from the fork branch, try
`git merge --no-commit upstream-import/X.Y.Z` on it (in a temporary
worktree, so the working tree of `repo` is not touched), abort the merge,
and write a Markdown report to `output` (default
`merge-plan-<name>-X.Y.Z.md` in the current directory).

"Deleted by us" conflicts on `fork_excluded_paths` are reported as
expected, apart from the real conflicts, and so are the files upstream added
under `fork_excluded_paths` (merged without a conflict). Files added
elsewhere are listed, for the fork's build. With `resolve_expected`, the merge
is not aborted: it is left in progress in `worktree` (default
[`default_sync_worktree`](@ref)) with the expected conflicts resolved by
`git rm` and the real ones still marked. Nothing is committed or pushed.
Refuses a local fork branch that differs from `origin`'s unless
`allow_stale`.

### `export_changes`

export_changes(u; repo, io=nothing, output=nothing) -> ExportReport

List our changes to the upstream sources: the commits on the fork branch
that are not on the upstream branch and touch `export_paths` (minus
`export_exclude`; with `export_modified_only`, only modifications of
existing files count), oldest first, with their GitHub URLs, plus the
diffstat of `upstream...fork` on the same paths. The Markdown is written
to `output` and/or printed to `io` when given.

## Results

### `UpstreamSync.CheckResult`

CheckResult

Outcome of [`check`](@ref): the upstream `releases`, the `latest` release
version, the versions already `imported` (from `upstream/X.Y.Z` tags),
the latest of them (`imported`, or `nothing`), and `new_release`.

### `UpstreamSync.ImportResult`

ImportResult

Outcome of [`import_release`](@ref): the new `commit` and its `branch`,
the `tag` that [`tag_release`](@ref) will create once the pull request is
merged, the source `url` and `checksum`, the `parent` commit (the upstream
branch), and the tarball paths `dropped` because they fall in a kept path.

### `UpstreamSync.TagResult`

TagResult

Outcome of [`tag_release`](@ref): the annotated `tag` on `commit` (of the
upstream branch, `ref`), whose tree is the import `tree`; `how` tells how
the commit was found.

### `UpstreamSync.MergePlan`

MergePlan

Outcome of [`merge_plan`](@ref). `changes` are the upstream file changes,
`overlap` the upstream-changed files that the fork also modified,
`conflicts` the real conflicts left by `git merge`, `expected` the
"deleted by us" conflicts on `fork_excluded_paths` (resolved by keeping the
deletion), `excluded_additions` the files upstream added under
`fork_excluded_paths` (git merges them without a conflict; they are removed
like the expected conflicts), `new_files` the other files upstream added
(the fork's build may need to list them), `worktree` the directory holding the merge in progress (with
`resolve_expected`, else `nothing`), `markdown` the report.

### `UpstreamSync.FileChange`

FileChange(path, status, added, deleted, area)

One file changed upstream between two imports (`status`: `A`, `M`, `D`,
`T`; `added`/`deleted` lines, `-1` for binary files).

### `UpstreamSync.Conflict`

Conflict(path, status, area)

A file left conflicted by `git merge` (`status` such as "both modified",
"deleted by us").

### `UpstreamSync.ExportReport`

ExportReport

Outcome of [`export_changes`](@ref): our `commits` touching the upstream
sources, the `diffstat` of `upstream...fork` on those paths, and the
`markdown` report.

### `UpstreamSync.CommitInfo`

CommitInfo(hash, date, subject, url, files)

## Configuration

### `UpstreamSync.Upstream`

Upstream

One fork and its upstream, as configured in `upstreams.toml` (see the
comments in that file for the meaning of every field).

### `UpstreamSync.load_config`

load_config(path = default_config_path()) -> Dict{String,Upstream}

### `UpstreamSync.default_config_path`

default_config_path() -> String

The `upstreams.toml` shipped at the root of this project.

### `UpstreamSync.get_upstream`

get_upstream(config, name) -> Upstream

### `UpstreamSync.fork_excluded`

fork_excluded(u, path) -> Bool

Whether `path` is one of the upstream files that the fork branch
intentionally does not carry (`fork_excluded_paths`, patterns as in
[`pathmatch`](@ref)).

### `UpstreamSync.cache_dir`

cache_dir() -> String

Download cache: `$UPSTREAM_SYNC_CACHE`, or `cache/` at the project root
(ignored by git). Tarballs are stored as `<cache>/<name>/<file>`.

## Building blocks

### `UpstreamSync.Release`

Release(version, filename)

An upstream release found in the download directory index.

### `UpstreamSync.parse_index`

parse_index(html, regex) -> Vector{Release}

Releases listed in an (Apache-style) directory index: every link whose
file name matches `regex`, whose first capture group is the `X.Y.Z`
version. Sorted by version, one entry per version.

### `UpstreamSync.latest_release`

latest_release(releases) -> Union{Release, Nothing}

### `UpstreamSync.parse_version`

parse_version(s) -> VersionNumber

Parse a strict `X.Y.Z` release version (no `v` prefix, no suffix).

### `UpstreamSync.is_newer`

is_newer(latest, imported) -> Bool

Whether the `latest` upstream release is newer than the `imported` one.
`nothing` means "no release" (`latest`) or "nothing imported yet"
(`imported`).

### `UpstreamSync.parse_upstream_tags`

parse_upstream_tags(ls_remote_output, prefix) -> Vector{VersionNumber}

Versions of the `refs/tags/<prefix>X.Y.Z` tags in the output of
`git ls-remote --tags`, sorted and unique. Peeled entries (`^{}`) and
non-version tags are ignored.

### `UpstreamSync.imported_versions`

imported_versions(u; repo=nothing) -> Vector{VersionNumber}

Versions of the `upstream/X.Y.Z` tags, read with `git ls-remote --tags`
from `repo` (a path or URL) or, by default, from the GitHub repository.

### `UpstreamSync.parse_checksums`

parse_checksums(text) -> Dict{String,String}

Parse a `md5sum`/`sha256sum`-style file (`<hex>  <file>` or
`<hex> *<file>` per line) into `file => lower-case hex`.

### `UpstreamSync.file_digest`

file_digest(path, algorithm) -> String

Lower-case hexadecimal digest of a file (`md5`, `sha1`, `sha256`, `sha512`).

### `UpstreamSync.checksum_ok`

checksum_ok(path, expected, algorithm) -> Bool

### `UpstreamSync.verify_checksum`

verify_checksum(path, filename, checksums, algorithm) -> String

Check `path` against `checksums[filename]`; return the digest. Throws
[`ChecksumMismatch`](@ref) on mismatch and [`UpstreamSyncError`](@ref) if
`filename` has no published checksum.

### `UpstreamSync.fetch_text`

fetch_text(url) -> String

### `UpstreamSync.fetch_release`

fetch_release(u, version; cache, offline=false, io=stdout)

Download (or reuse from the cache) the release tarball and the checksum
file, and verify the checksum. The checksum file is always refreshed unless
`offline`; a cached tarball that no longer matches is downloaded again once
(upstream sometimes re-uploads a release under the same name). Returns
`(; url, path, filename, checksum)`.

### `UpstreamSync.extract_tarball`

extract_tarball(tarball, workdir) -> String

Extract with the system `tar` into a fresh directory below `workdir` and
return the tarball's single top-level directory.

### `UpstreamSync.tarball_executables`

tarball_executables(tarball) -> Set{String}

Regular files of the tarball (top directory stripped) whose owner execute
bit is set in the tar header. The extracted files are not trusted for this:
some file systems (ACL or network mounts) report every file as executable.

### `UpstreamSync.build_tree`

build_tree(repo, root, keep_paths, upstream_sha; executables=nothing)
        -> (tree, dropped)

Write a git tree with the exact bytes of every file below `root` (no
`.gitattributes`/`.gitignore`/eol filtering), with the `keep_paths` taken
from `upstream_sha` instead. File modes are 100755 for the paths in
`executables` (default: the owner execute bit on disk). Uses a temporary
index: the working tree and the real index of `repo` are not touched.

### `UpstreamSync.tag_message`

tag_message(u, version, import_message) -> String

The message of the `upstream/X.Y.Z` tag: the source URL and checksum lines
of the import commit message.

### `UpstreamSync.export_pathspecs`

export_pathspecs(u) -> Vector{String}

Git pathspecs for "our fixes": `export_paths` minus `export_exclude`
(git glob pathspecs, e.g. `**/meson.build`).

### `UpstreamSync.Area`

Area of the tree a file belongs to, used to group merge conflicts.
Values: `Area.BUILD`, `Area.SRC`, `Area.DOCS`, `Area.OTHER`.

### `UpstreamSync.area_title`

area_title(area) -> String

### `UpstreamSync.pathmatch`

pathmatch(pattern, path) -> Bool

Match a repository path against a pattern:

- `dir/` (trailing slash) matches everything below `dir/`;
- a pattern containing `/` is a glob on the whole path (`*`, `?`, `**`);
- a pattern without `/` is a glob on the file name (`meson.build`,
  `*.md`), at any depth;
- a leading `/` anchors the pattern at the root (`/configure` matches
  `configure` only, `/mk*` matches `mkosx` but not `src/mkfoo`).

### `UpstreamSync.classify`

classify(path, areas) -> Area.T

First area (in the order build, src, docs) with a matching pattern;
`Area.OTHER` otherwise. `areas` maps `"build"`, `"src"`, `"docs"` to
pattern lists (see [`pathmatch`](@ref)).

### `UpstreamSync.run_git`

run_git(args; dir=nothing, input=nothing, env=nothing) -> GitResult

Run `git [-C dir] args...` without throwing, capturing stdout and stderr.

### `UpstreamSync.git`

git(repo, args...; input=nothing, env=nothing) -> String

Run git in `repo`; return stdout without the trailing newline; throw an
[`UpstreamSyncError`](@ref) if git fails.

### `UpstreamSync.resolve_branch`

resolve_branch(repo, branch) -> (ref, sha)

A local branch `refs/heads/<branch>`, or else `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>`.

### `UpstreamSync.check_not_stale`

check_not_stale(repo, branch, ref, sha; allow_stale=false, io=stdout,
                    remote="origin")

Refuse to work from a local `branch` (resolved to `ref` at `sha`) that
differs from the same branch on `remote` (read with `git ls-remote`), unless
`allow_stale`. Without such a remote, or if the remote has no such branch,
only a note is printed.

### `UpstreamSync.try_merge`

try_merge(repo, sync, import_ref, wt; keep=false, resolve=raw -> String[])
        -> Vector{(path, code)}

`git merge --no-commit import_ref` in a new worktree `wt` of branch `sync`
and return the conflicted paths with their porcelain codes. Without `keep`
the merge is aborted and the worktree removed. With `keep`, the paths
returned by `resolve(conflicts)` are `git rm`-ed and the worktree is left
with the merge in progress.

Returns `(conflicts, added)`, `added` being the paths the merge adds to
`sync` without a conflict. With `keep`, the paths returned by
`resolve(conflicts, added)` are `git rm`-ed.

### `UpstreamSync.default_sync_worktree`

default_sync_worktree(u, version, repo) -> String

Where `merge-plan --resolve-expected` leaves the merge: `<repo>-sync-X.Y.Z`
next to the clone.

## Errors

### `UpstreamSync.UpstreamSyncError`

UpstreamSyncError(msg)

A user-facing error (bad configuration, missing branch, network failure,
...). The CLI prints the message and exits with status 1 (see [`ExitCode`](@ref)).

### `UpstreamSync.ChecksumMismatch`

ChecksumMismatch(file, algorithm, expected, actual)

The downloaded `file` does not have the checksum published upstream.
